q: Ipocras seems to have been a great favourite with our ancestors, being served up at every entertainment, public or private.

1846, James Orchard Halliwell, “IPOCRAS”, in A Dictionary of Archaic and Provincial Words, Obsolete Phrases, Proverbs, and Ancient Customs, from the Fourteenth Century. […], volume I (A–I), London: Jo

e: Probably from Greek ιππότης (ippótis, “knight”), which is derived from ίππος (íppos, “horse”).
